sanity.question: How often does the weather station save a reading?

Passages:

[1] Backyard weather station: overview
The backyard weather station sits on a fence post behind the shed. It measures air temperature, humidity, air pressure and wind speed. A small board wakes up every ten minutes, takes one reading of each sensor, writes it as a line of text to a memory card and goes back to sleep. Once an hour it also joins the home wifi and uploads the last six lines to a personal server, so the chart on the page is never more than an hour old. The first version saved a reading every minute, but the memory card filled up in a few weeks, so the interval was changed.

[2] Backyard weather station: the mast
The wind sensor is a three cup anemometer fixed to the top of a two metre wooden mast, well above the fence so that the shed does not shelter it. The cups spin a small magnet past a switch, and the board counts the pulses over a few seconds to get a speed. The mast is held by two guy wires and has been through two winter storms without moving. The temperature and humidity sensor lives in a white stack of plastic plates that shades it from direct sun and still lets the air through.

[3] Sourdough diary: feeding the starter
The sourdough starter lives in a glass jar on the kitchen shelf and is fed once a day with equal weights of flour and water. Before each feeding most of it is thrown away, so the jar never holds more than about a hundred grams. A rubber band around the jar marks the level, which makes it easy to see how far the starter rose overnight. In winter it rises slowly and gets a warmer spot near the oven; in summer it can double within four hours and is kept in the fridge between bakes.

[4] Station power and enclosure
The electronics sit in a grey plastic box with a gasket lid, screwed to the post under a small roof of corrugated plastic. A solar panel the size of a paperback charges a single lithium battery through a charge controller. Because the board sleeps almost all the time, the battery lasted through a whole week of cloud in November without dropping below half. Cable glands keep rain out where the sensor wires enter the box, and a packet of silica gel inside the lid is replaced each spring.
